Bengaluru City in Crl.Misc.No.9385/2023 wherein, anticipatory bail has been granted to respondent Nos.2 and 3 herein in Crime No.362/2023 registered by Subramanyapura Police Station, Benglauru City for the offences punishable under Sections 341, 323, 354, 504 and 506 of IPC.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
3. The de-facto complainant has approached this Court challenging the order passed by learned Sessions Judge in Crl.Misc.No.9385/2023 principally on two grounds.

First ground is that the de-facto complainant was not made a party to Crl.Misc.No.9385/2023 and the second ground is that the NC: 2023:KHC:41291 learned Sessions Judge, has not given cogent reasons for grant of anticipatory bail to respondent Nos.2 and 3.
4.

FIR in Crime No.362/2023 was registered by Subramanyapura Police Station, Bengaluru City against respondent Nos.2 and 3 for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 323, 341, 504 and 506 of IPC on the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner herein.

Section 439(1A) of Cr.P.C.
provides that the presence of the informant or any person authorized by him shall be obligatory at the time of hearing of the application for bail to the accused under sub- section (3) of section 376 or Smt. sentences.text: FIR in the present case has not been registered for any of the offences mentioned in Section 439(1A) of Cr.P.C.
Except for the offence covered under Section 439(1A) of Cr.P.C., there is no requirement in law for making the victim as a party to the bail application.

5. It is trite that in the event, the victim makes an application before the Court in which application is filed by the accused seeking anticipatory bail or regular bail, the said Court shall grant an opportunity of hearing to the victim.

NC: 2023:KHC:41291 Undisputedly, the petitioner has not made any such application before the Trial Court in Crl.Misc.No.9385/2023 and in the absence of making any such application, the petitioner cannot put-forward a grievance that she was not heard in the matter.
6. The second ground urged by learned counsel for the petitioner is that the Trial Court has not assigned appropriate reasons for granting anticipatory bail to respondent Nos.2 and 3.
Undisputedly, FIR in the present case has been filed against respondent Nos.2 and 3 for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 323, 341, 504 and 506 of IPC.
The alleged offences are trialbe by the Court of Magistrate and the maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment for five years.
Considering this aspect of the matter, the Trial Court has granted anticipatory bail to respondent Nos.2 and 3.

Therefore, I do not find any force in the contention urged by learned counsel for the petitioner that the learned Sessions Judge has not assigned appropriate reasons for granting anticipatory bail to respondent Nos.2 and 3.
It is trite that bail granted to an accused can be cancelled only in exceptional or supervening circumstances.

In the present case, no such exceptional or supervening circumstance is pointed out by the NC:
2023:KHC:41291 learned counsel for the petitioner, which needs interference as against the order of anticipatory bail granted by the learned Sessions Judge in Crl. Misc. No.9385/2023 in favour of respondent Nos.2 and 3 in Crime No.362/2023 registered by Subramanyapura Police Station,
Bengaluru City.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petition is bereft of merits and is accordingly, dismissed.

Sd/-
